# Implementation TODO — live progress board

> Index: [README](README.md) · Spec: [`dacode-design.md`](../dacode-design.md) ·
> Decisions: [Appendix B](appendices/B-decisions.md) ·
> Spec deltas: [Appendix A](appendices/A-design-deltas.md)

**What this file is.** The durable answer to *"what is done, what is next, what
is blocked"*. The other docs hold content — [README](README.md) is the index,
[Appendix B](appendices/B-decisions.md) holds decision reasoning,
[Appendix A](appendices/A-design-deltas.md) holds proposed spec edits. This file
holds **state**, and it is the only place that should be edited when something
merely *changes status*.

It replaced the session-scoped `todo-followup.md` handoff note at the repo root.
That file is **deleted**: every one of its 11 unchecked entries was verified
mirrored here (and §6 is a superset), and its own Track B tables had gone stale —
they listed B1–B13 when 14 existed and A1–A16 when 17 did, so a cold reader
trusting it would have worked from a dead decision list. `git log --
todo-followup.md` is the session-1/2/3 narrative.

**Maintenance rules.**
- A status change is a one-line edit here. Reasoning goes in the appendix or the
  feature doc, not here.
- Strike resolved items, never delete — the audit trail matters.
- §6 items carry a stable id (`U1`, `U2`, …) so one can be **cited and closed**
  rather than restated. **Never renumber**: a new item takes the next unused
  number wherever it sits in the file, so gaps are normal and meaningful. The id
  lives inside the leading bold run, after the checkbox, because checking an item
  off must not change a value a tool reads — `attention.py` keys on it.
- Flip a feature doc's `migrated summary; expand during implementation` marker to
  `expanded` **only when it is actually deepened**, so the counts below stay
  greppable:
  `grep -rl "migrated summary; expand during implementation" docs/implementation --exclude=TODO.md | wc -l`.
  **Grep the full phrase, not the two words — both halves are load-bearing.** The
  `--exclude` because this file quotes the marker; the full phrase because *any*
  prose mentioning the marker in passing would otherwise count as carrying it.
  The short form silently reported 28 during the B1 pass, when an Appendix B
  banner said a doc was "still a migrated summary" — describing the marker is not
  the same as bearing it.
- Keep §1's blocker list honest. An item that has been "blocked" for three
  sessions is either not blocked or not wanted.

> (**secondary APPROVE at round 1; primary REQUEST CHANGES → APPROVE at round 2**, its six findings all
> discharged and each re-measured rather than taken on trust). **[A28](appendices/A-design-deltas.md)**
> carries the spec half: §3.2's `DenyReason` and `Deny { reason: Option<DenyReason> }`, §3.3's arm list,
> §4.3 naming `decision.reason` as the mechanism, and §4.4's three corrections — the **three pattern
> domains** stated per key, `.env` → `**/.env` with the anchoring rule, and **a `deny` is a floor** no
> session grant or mode overrides, with the mode mapping the section had left implicit.
>
> **The refinement is the part worth keeping, and it came from the pass that built the thing rather than
> from the ruling.** Arm (a) as recommended was non-optional, which puts a *diagnostic* on the **command**
> path: every client answering `ResolvePermission` with a denial would have to name an engine taxonomy
> whose only correct value there is a constant. `Option` removes the burden without a sixth `Client` arm,
> because **`None` *is* the answerer case**, corroborated by `PermissionResolved.by`. The implementer found
> it, not the ruling — the same shape as R-f/R-g at M1.6 Pass A.
>
> ⚠️ **And one of the three reasons I gave the user for arm (a) was measured false, one turn after I gave
> it.** I argued a `Snapshot` fold could not see an event-side field; `fold.rs` handles
> `PermissionResolved` as `answered(snapshot, req)` — it **discards** the decision — and `Snapshot` retains
> no permission decisions at all, so arm (b) would have satisfied §4.3 fully. The arm survives on the two
> reasons that are true (`dacode-core`'s `PermissionResolution` carries a decision to its waiter without the
> event; a field on `PermissionResolved` would spend lines `event.rs` does not have). Recorded rather than
> dropped, because it is the board's own recurring class — *a deferral's reason is what the next pass acts
> on* — arriving in a recommendation rather than in a deferral.
>
> ⚠️ **The same correction applies to doc 16 §16.13's gate 2, which this board's own M1.6 framing fed it.**
> It warned that a reason-carrying `Deny` would not fit beside `event.rs`'s **998** lines. `PermDecision`
> does not live in `event.rs` — it lives in `perm.rs` (188 lines) and `event.rs` only *references* the type,
> so arm (a) cost that file **zero** lines and no split was needed. The hazard is real but belongs to
> whichever row next adds an `Event` **variant or field** — and **U166** is a candidate to do exactly that.
>
> **`{"type":"Deny"}` → `{"type":"Deny","data":{}}` is the delta register's first golden diff.** Adjacent

> round for its four NITs. **26 mutations, 22 killed by assertion, 4 declared survivors — all four judged
> legitimate.** U133 and U135 **closed**; U123's seam-and-contract half landed (mechanism still conditional
> on U136); U134's *recording* half landed and the decision stays M1.9's; debt **d5** discharged with a
> documented deviation; **U137/U138/U139** filed with owners.
>
> ⚠️ **The finding worth carrying is not in the code: this pass shipped a flake, and every gate was green.**
> Round 1 passed the whole matrix and the primary's first `cargo test -p dacode-core` exited **101** — it
> measured **10 failures in 628 runs (~1.6%)** across three tests. Both causes were one shape: **a cross-task
> ordering asserted through an observation point that is not a happens-before edge.** Two tests read
> `events.jsonl` directly instead of through the flushing helper, because `apply` broadcasts *inside* `emit`
> and flushes only after; a third asserted an empty subscriber queue the instant `send` returned, which holds
> only while `writer.append().await` happens to yield. A 1.6% flake hides with probability ≈0.984 *per run*,
> so "every gate exits 0" was true and meant nothing.
>
> ⚠️ **And fixing it introduced a second flake pointing the other way.** The re-fence that converted a hang
> into an assertion bounded a wait on `LogWriter::shutdown` — whose work runs on a **blocking-pool thread**
> doing a real drain + flush + `fsync`, so the bound was spent by the *observer* and not consumed by the
> *observed*. The primary measured **8/160 failures at 8 concurrent workers** with 1- and 2-worker runs clean.
> **The two flakes were load-sensitive in opposite directions** (the first needed a *fast* writer reply and
> reproduced at 1 worker; the second needed a *starved* blocking pool and reproduced only at ≥4), which is why
> no single repeat count catches both. Fixed by raising that one bound 25× with the reason written down and
> the failure message naming **two** causes plus the discriminator between them; the primary then re-ran
> **1020 runs across five load levels, 0 failures**, including 0/240 at the same 8-worker saturation that had
> produced 8/160. **Consequence for the gate matrix (tracker f182/f184): it gains a REPEAT gate (N≥200 at 1
> worker) and a CONTENTION gate (≥4 concurrent whole-suite workers)** over whichever modules carry cross-task
> ordering — **derived per pass, not hardcoded**, because that membership changes — **with the detection floor
> stated** (1−(1−p)^N: 96% at p=1.6%, 63% at p=0.5%, 18% at p=0.1%) so a green REPEAT reads as "not detected at
> this N" and never as "absent". A related rule: any new bounded-yield loop must say **what it gates on**, and
> if the answer is "a blocking-pool or `std` thread" its bound is not comparable to the others'.
>
> ⚠️ **The second recurring class: a deferral's *reason* is what the next pass acts on, and twice the reason
> was false.** (i) Round 2 asserted the pump "has no way to bound an `.await` without tokio's `time` feature"
> — while the bounded-yield-plus-`is_finished` pattern appeared **four times in that same diff**. (ii) Round 3
> justified leaving two cancel races untested by claiming a test would need production surface that does not
> exist; measured, `StoreFactory`, `OpenedStore` (both fields `pub`), `EventStore` and `LogWriter::spawn` are
> all `pub`, so a test-local double costs ~40 lines and **zero** production surface — and the cited precedent
> was a false analogy, U131 being two adjacent `sync` calls with no function boundary at any visibility.
> **Both conclusions survived; both recorded reasons did not**, and a wrong reason is what a later pass
> declines a cheap test on. Filed as **U137** (M3's). The generalisation is now in `.agents/pitfalls-live.md`:
> *"cannot be done without X" has two flavours needing different greps — a missing **mechanism** (grep the
> current diff for the pattern) and a missing **seam** (grep the crate for the visibility of the named
> boundary)* — and for the seam flavour the question is not "is it `pub`" but "**can a `#[cfg(test)]` child of
> the module that needs it reach it**", which `SessionRegistry`'s own `pub(crate)` answers *no* for and is why
> `registry_tests.rs` spawns child processes by name instead of living in `crates/dacode-core/tests/`.

> CHANGES (narrow) → APPROVE** across four implementer rounds, with the final

> ⚠️ **Four questions were settled at the opening, and three of them were holes
> rather than choices — which is why they were asked instead of built.** **U117**
> was a hard gate: §3.6 specified a per-field compression discriminator and §14.1
> mandates three tests over it at this row, but **no section anywhere gave the
> field's on-disk shape**, and line 1 carries `format_version: 1`, so whatever was
> written would have been pinned by it. Ruled (option 1 of four): a sibling
> `<leaf>_codec` key whose **absence means `plain`**, the compressed value being
> base64 — decided by the property that an *uncompressed* record is then
> byte-identical to the wire encoding, so `compress = "off"` and `JsonlStore`'s
> `"blobs"` default both yield a log any client can fold with no store-side
> transform. **U118** was the same shape for a torn log tail: nothing said what an
> opener does, and A1's first answer (refuse) would have made a mid-write crash
> permanently brick a session that §3.6's kernel-owns-the-lock design exists to
> reopen — ruled (b), truncate to the last complete line, fsync, proceed, report
> the bytes. **f120's second half** and **f138** (are the traits sync?) both
> resolved from spec facts rather than preference: §13.5's two-axes sentence puts
> the compression *level* in config and not on `Codec`, and §5.1's own backend table
> puts the second implementor at M3 as a *local embedded* library while §7.4's
> writer is a `std` thread that cannot `.await`.
>
> ⚠️ **The review's HIGH was demonstrated by running code, and its root cause was
> the doc, not the code.** `validated_prefix` walked back from the tail and
> accepted everything before the first record that validated, on a stated
> assumption that *"the corruption model is a lost suffix"* — true of a crash,
> false of a corruption. A damaged offset in the **middle** of `index.bin`
> therefore silently renumbered `events.jsonl`, **inverting §12's asymmetry** (the
> rebuildable projection damaging the file that is the truth) and minting phantom
> cursors while reporting a **clean** `LogRecovery`, persistently across a reopen.
> Doc 05 §5.5's invariant 3 had said *"validate **the last record**"* and the code
> transcribed it faithfully. **That is the third time this milestone has found the
> defect in a plan doc rather than in the code that followed it**, and the lesson is
> the one §5.4's division of labour implies: a plan doc that states a *mechanism*
> is transcribed, so a wrong mechanism is reproduced exactly. The fix went into
> §5.5 first and the code followed — O(1) verification at the two points of use
> plus an in-memory arithmetic sweep, because verifying every record at open costs
> what a rebuild costs and would leave the index pointless.
>
> **Two lessons recorded where the next pass will meet them.** First, **a
> reviewer's context is sometimes the only diff available**: `index.rs`'s 301-line
> test module was moved out to get under the cap, and the implementer could not
> byte-diff the move because `store/` was untracked — so it offered an
> indentation-asserting extraction script, a `--list` diff, a green suite and eight
> mutations, **none of which can distinguish "moved" from "moved and quietly
> weakened", because a dropped assertion leaves all of them green**. The primary had
> round 1's file verbatim in context and diffed it assertion-by-assertion. ⚠️ **The
> operational consequence for A2 is a sequencing rule, not a caveat**: `jsonl.rs` is
> now committed, so a split of *its* test module has a git baseline — **commit the
> split on its own, before the compression work**, and the move becomes verifiable
> by anyone instead of only by a reviewer who happens to hold the prior text.
> Second, **"unreachable today" arithmetic is not a shrug when the release failure
> is silence rather than a crash**: an unguarded `until - window.from` panics in
> debug but in release wraps, becomes `read_to_end`, and the limit `break`
> truncates to the *right* record — so `read_range` returned `Ok` with exactly the
> envelope asked for, and a production caller would never learn the projection lied
> or trigger the rebuild. `clippy::arithmetic_side_effects` is **not** among doc
> 04's six, so no gate ever catches the class; the sweep of all eight production
> subtractions in `store/` found the other six provably guarded (f150).

> ### ✅ 2026-09-19 — A7 applied: the auth and path-safety surface, and two rules the delta did not contain
>
> **The first transcription of a new session and the largest of the queue** — ten spec
> sections against the two A7's entry named (§8.2, §8.3, §8.4, §8.5, §3.6, §3.7, §5.1,
> §9.2, §12, §14), because each of its three parts needed a section the entry did not
> list. **§8.2 grew from 16 routes to 23**, and the scaling axis is normative there —
> which is what makes **two existing citations resolve to content instead of to a
> heading**: §2.2 (A13) and §3.7 (A14) both already pointed at "§8.2's storage and auth
> traits", and §8.2 described none. ⚠️ **That is the `§14.2` hazard class one level
> subtler, and `check_section_refs()` cannot see it**: the gate checks that a `§N.M`
> reference resolves, and §8.2 resolves. A reference can be *valid and empty*. The only
> thing that found it was reading the cited section for the content the citer claimed —
> which is a procedure, not a gate, and it is now the second manual sweep this board owes
> a name to.
>
> **Its own gate was not transcribed, because it is incoherent.** A7's proposal says
> config writes are "gated on controller status (§8.4)". §5.1's four layers are built-in
> defaults, user config, repo config and env/CLI — **none session-scoped** — while §8.4's
> controller rule reaches only commands that *mutate a session*. A14 had already ruled on
> exactly this for the registry, and A22 assigned A7 the single answer covering all three
> surfaces, so §8.4 now states **one rule for every non-session write** rather than a gate
> per endpoint. **The seam was wrong too**: §8.4 said the rule "lands" on `Hello`'s reserved
> capability flags, but **`Hello` is not a `Command`** — it is §7.2's extension handshake —
> so a flag there cannot gate a browser and a tenant cannot gate a bridge. §8.3 now names
> both seams and requires one policy.
>
> ⚠️ **Two rules A7 does not contain were added, and both are in the class this board says
> no gate can catch — a rule that is too permissive.**
>
> 1. **The writable root is derived server-side and never supplied.** One server
>    legitimately hosts sessions in several repositories (`CreateSession` carries a `cwd`,
>    §4.7 maps worktrees), so "`<repo>/.dacode/`" has **no single referent**. A client-named
>    root would let a browser working in repo A write repo B's config, and an ambiguous root
>    would make §8.5's allowlist decorative — it would be checking a path nobody pinned down.
>    So: `?layer=user` → `~/.config/dacode/`; `?layer=repo` → the server's cwd or a named
>    session's cwd. **No request field carries a path.**
> 2. **A write may not add an exec surface.** `[[extensions]]`' `cmd` (§7.2) and a hook's
>    `run`/`post` (§7.1) are **refused although the file holding them is inside the
>    allowlist**, because at those keys editing configuration *is* executing code — as the
>    server's user, at every later start, from a file that outlives the request. The
>    composition is A22's shape again: §9.2 renders model-authored markdown on the
>    authenticated origin, so a script that reaches that origin could turn **one transcript
>    into persistent command execution**. It costs the *operator* nothing (`dacode config
>    edit` in a terminal still reaches those keys) and constrains only a client acting on
>    their behalf — the distinction the user settled A22's item 2 on, reused rather than
>    reinvented.
>
> **Four more decisions, each with its reason in the spec.** Writes are **conditional**
> (`ETag` on every read, `If-Match` required, `412` on mismatch) because four writers reach
> one file — a browser, `dacode config edit`, the user's editor, and §4.8's promotion — and
> "a human reviews the diff" is not a reconciliation mechanism for a clobber. The board route
> is **repo-scoped, following the file** (§12), resolving against the server's cwd and
> returning `409` outside a repository; the project-level reading survives as *presentation*
> (§9.2) and not as a second routing axis. **`promote` is two checks** — controller-gated at
> the session owning the item, allowlist- and `If-Match`-gated at the path — and from the
> model a promotion is a **write through §4.4** (§4.8's `Verify::Command` rule is the
> precedent) while from a browser it is not a tool call at all, so neither door inherits the
> other's check. **No `POST`**: the client names the file, so create and replace are one
> idempotent operation, which is §3.3's caller-allocated-id reasoning applied to HTTP.
>
> **U99 closed, and its socket half is a compatibility event.** `org_version` on all four
> tree reads — §12's monotonic `version`, stored rather than derived from mtime because mtime
> is not monotonic across a rename-on-write, a restore, or two hosts sharing a home directory,
> and a freshness token that can go backwards silently makes a client that trusts it stale
> forever — plus **§3.6's third down-frame kind, `Hint`**. It is not an `Envelope` and gets
> **no golden fixture**, because §14.1 derives the fixture set from `Event`'s variants: no
> `session`, no `seq`, no cursor, never written, never replayed, safe to lose, since the
> authoritative version travels on the read it prompts. That is exactly the line §3.7 draws,
> so the registry does not become an event stream.
>
> **Debt created, with owners.** ⚠️ **B10 is now half-applied**: its comment-preserving
> writes are **normative at §5.1** — where §12 already cited them and no section carried
> them, so before this pass the requirement existed in the spec only as a *citation* — while
> its generated `dacode.schema.json` stays owed to A12/doc 17, and **B10 must not be marked
> applied**. That schema now has a constraint: §8.5 refuses the exec-bearing keys, so a
> config schema is **not** the write endpoints' schema. **`xtask` has three generators to
> specify** if all land (B6's tool schema, B2's protocol schema, B10's config schema), and
> doc 01 §1.5's register row owes that. **Docs 19, 20, 17, 18, 21 and 32 each carried a line
> A7 falsified** and were corrected under hard rule 1 with their markers untouched — **doc
> 21's two stale §9.1 lines were A8's leftover, found here rather than left standing**. **Two
> new §6 items: U103** (§3.3 has no task-mutation `Command`, so the browser path to `promote`
> and to closing a `Verify::Manual` item does not exist in the protocol) and **U104** (what a
> config write does to a *running* session is undecided — §5.6 owns re-assembly timing and
> §4.5 the cache consequence). **The inbound-assignment sweep's scope was too narrow again**:
> doc 06 §6.4 carries A7 work as "**[DESIGN DELTA §8.2 / A7]**" — the four organization reads
> — and the sweep greps Appendices A, B and TODO §6, not the plan docs, so it reported clean
> over an unfulfilled assignment for the second time.

> ### ✅ 2026-09-18 — A8 applied: a deferral with its prerequisite un-conditioned, and a contradiction nobody had flagged
>
> **The twelfth transcription of the day, and the smallest** — one spec section (§9.1)
> plus a correction to doc 03. It was taken ahead of A7 for a specific reason: A7 is M3
> scope with two genuinely open placement questions, while A8 fixes an **M1 deliverable
> that was sitting inside an M3 conditional**.
>
> **B2's split transcribed, and the framework deliberately NOT picked** — which is the
> whole discipline of this delta, since the split *is* the decision. §9.1 no longer says
> "Decision pending"; it says the framework is an **open decision with a deadline** (due by
> **M3**), with **TS SPA (Solid)** as the *standing recommendation* and both reasons
> recorded so the choice is not relitigated from scratch: all three reference web UIs
> chose TypeScript, and this UI's four hard parts (streaming markdown, highlighting,
> virtualised lists, diff rendering) have mature TS solutions and weak WASM ones. A
> recommendation is not a decision, so §9.2 and §9.3 stay framework-neutral. **Putting the
> deadline in the spec is what stops a deferral drifting** — previously it lived only in
> this board and Appendix B.
>
> ⚠️ **The prerequisite was conditional on the thing it was supposed to make cheap.** B2
> made the JSON-Schema export a **non-optional M1** deliverable, but §9.1 carried it *only*
> inside the "If TS:" branch, and doc 03 said outright "**Optional**: … **if** the web UI is
> a TS SPA". So an M1 obligation was gated on an M3 decision — and backwards, because **the
> export is what makes the TS branch cheap**, so requiring the branch first made the
> framework decision harder rather than easier. §9.1 now states that inversion explicitly
> and lists the export's framework-independent uses (extension authors validating a
> `Command`, a future SDK, `run --output jsonl` consumers, and §14.1's golden fixtures,
> which already pin the wire format in JSON and so are half a schema).
>
> **This is the fourth time a signed decision's M1 half was found sitting inside a
> conditional** — A25's wire half, A10's exchange-record carve-out, A21's dangling `§14.2`
> citations, and now this. That makes it a pattern to check for rather than a run of bad
> luck: **when a delta records a deferral with a committed prerequisite, check where the
> prerequisite currently lives**, because deferrals get written inside the branch they were
> carved out of and the prerequisite inherits the conditionality it was meant to escape.
>
> **A contradiction nobody had flagged, resolved by §13.3 and §2.4 rather than by choice.**
> §9.1's old text had "a `build.rs` step emits `protocol.d.ts` … via a small JSON-Schema
> export **in `dacode-protocol`**". But §13.3 confines `schemars` to an offline generator
> because it depends on `serde_json` non-optionally — **"never in a shipped crate"** — and
> §2.4 puts build-time codegen in **`xtask`** on the test of whether its output ships. So
> the generator is `xtask`'s, `dacode-protocol` grows neither a `schemars` dependency nor a
> `build.rs`, and `protocol.d.ts` is generated **in CI with a drift check that fails the
> build** — layered on the golden fixtures, which catch a change to the serialized shape
> while the drift check catches the generated types falling out of step with it, the one
> failure a second language cannot otherwise see. §9.1 names this as §14.1's existing
> `xtask` rule applied to a second generator, not as a new rule.
>
> **Doc 03's line was a false claim, not a stale marker**, so it was corrected under hard
> rule 1 with its summary marker and depth untouched — the same argument that justified
> correcting doc 08's `Dynamic(fn)` arm under A2. **Debt:** the framework decision itself,
> by M3; **doc 21** is still a summary so §9.1/§9.2/§9.3 are its normative source; and
> **`xtask` now has two generators to specify** (the tool-schema one from §13.3 and this
> one), which doc 01 §1.5's register row should reflect when M1 deepens it.

> ### ✅ 2026-09-18 — A22 applied: all four capability seams closed, and one redirect was reversed on purpose
>
> **The eleventh transcription of the day, and the one that closes the security seams.**
> Ten spec sections — §3.3, §4.4, §5.3, §7.1, §7.2, §8.2, §8.3, §8.4, §9.2, §14 — against
> the six the delta named, because item 4's link rule is a *renderer* rule belonging in
> §9.2, item 2's bound needed §3.3's `PermDecision` comment as well as §4.4, and every item
> needs §14 tests. **B7's confirmation of A23's `yolo` carve-out landed in the same pass**,
> as A22's banner required, so §4.4 was edited once rather than twice and **A23's debt is
> discharged**.
>
> ⚠️ **The headline is a reversal, and it was the user's.** At sign-off, item 2 was
> redirected to "permissive v1" and the banner recorded the `AllowPattern` subset bound as
> *part of what permissive declines* — flagged for redirect, with the argument written down
> in case it was wrong. **It was wrong, and the user redirected it back: the bound IS
> applied.** The argument that settled it is the one the flag anticipated — *permissive*
> describes the **user's** experience, and the bound does not touch it, since a user at
> their own terminal can still grant `**` explicitly. What the bound constrains is a **client
> acting on the user's behalf**. Without it, three separately-written rules compose into an
> escalation: §3.3's `AllowPattern(String)` injects a caller-chosen glob, §4.4 puts session
> grants at the **top** of the resolution order above agent/project/user config, and §8.4
> lets extensions resolve permissions regardless of control — so one bridge answering one
> prompt could grant `**` for the session, making any connected extension
> root-equivalent. The bound is mechanically checkable at resolution time because the
> request is already in `PermissionRequested { scope }`; a pattern outside it is an
> `Ack Err`. **The capability split stays reserved**, so §8.4's trust model is now stated
> explicitly (*a connected extension is as trusted as the local terminal*) and `Hello`
> reserves `answer_questions`/`resolve_permissions`, granted by default in v1 — B7's
> inert-stub pattern applied to a trust model.
>
> **The other three items landed as confirmed, each with the reason it is a rule rather
> than a preference.** **Item 1** (`U61`): `run` is an argv array executed **without a
> shell**, and **templating survives into argv elements** — deleting it would have been
> safer and less useful, while the array form keeps the convenience and removes the
> surface, so a title holding `; rm -rf ~` is one argument rather than a second command. A
> hook that wants a shell must write `["sh","-c",…]`, which is the point: the dangerous
> case becomes visible in the config instead of being the default behaviour of any hook
> that interpolates. §7.1 states *why* this is a rule and not an example-level detail —
> the example's own fields are client-controlled, but the natural fields to interpolate on
> `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested` (the prompt, a tool name, an error message) are
> **model-authored**, so `"{{ prompt }}"` in a shell string is a model-reachable
> command-injection bug and nothing about the field name warns the author. **Item 3**
> (`U64`): inheritance is an **intersection** — child scopes ∩ parent's, mode
> `min(child, parent)` — which makes §5.3's *existing* promise true on both axes instead of
> only the mode axis, and is not a restriction on an operator who can set the parent wide.
> **Item 4** (`U65`): `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` origin-wide, `rel="noopener
> noreferrer"` as a renderer rule, `?token=` documented as bootstrap-only and stripped once
> the cookie is set, and `/file` + `/blob/:blob_id` served as `text/plain` with
> `Content-Disposition: attachment` under a CSP forbidding inline script — both return
> arbitrary repository or tool content **on the authenticated origin**, which is a
> stored-XSS delivery path. §8.3 records that none of this costs capability, which is why
> it was never part of the permissive trade-off: what stops leaking is dacode's **own**
> bearer token.
>
> **`yolo` was confirmed and then improved.** The carve-out stands — a mode whose whole
> meaning is that the user opted out of being asked cannot start asking, and a mode that
> silently becomes `ask` under one condition is a mode nobody can reason about, which is
> consistent with B7's polarity amendment making `yolo` the deliberate mutable opt-out.
> Auditability was never lost, since the detection is still recorded on
> `PermissionResolved`. **But `yolo` is also the mode where a leak is *most* likely** —
> everything runs automatically, so nothing passes a human on the way to exec — and
> therefore the one mode where an escalation-based warning would never fire. So the first
> detection in a session raises a **non-blocking notice**: rendered once, pausing nothing,
> requiring no answer, not repeated. Once per session rather than per detection, because a
> notice on every occurrence in a mode chosen for not being interrupted *would be* the
> interruption.
>
> **Closed: U61, U62, U64, U65 — four items, and U62's closure corrected its own
> annotation**, which had said "do not close this item on A22's account; it moved" and "the
> escalation is documented and made reversible, **not fixed**". Both were true when written
> and false now, so they are struck rather than left standing. **U63 stays open and was
> checked rather than assumed**: §4.4's main `bash` allow-list being advisory is B7's
> wording, and A22's entry says explicitly that correcting it would pre-empt B7 — so it
> remains B7's owed transcription, not A22's.
>
> **Debt created, with owners.** **A25's M5 half** inherits §8.4's trust model and must
> argue capabilities for a *remote* principal **on its own merits**, since the split no
> longer arrives from here — §7.2's reserved flags are the mechanism it should use. ~~**A7**
> owns §8.5's writable-path allowlist and "who may `promote` from a browser", and should
> answer it together with A14's **U99** registry question rather than separately, because
> §8.4 now says the rule for non-session writes should be decided **once**.~~ ✅ **A7
> discharged both on 2026-09-19, and did answer them together**: §8.5 has the allowlist,
> §8.4 has the one rule for every non-session write, `promote` is two checks, and **U99 is
> closed**. ⚠️ **One correction this debt note could not have anticipated**: it names
> "§7.2's reserved flags" as the mechanism A25's M5 half should use, but **`Hello` is not a
> `Command`** — it is the extension handshake — so flags there cannot gate a *browser* or a
> *remote* principal. §8.3 now names **two seams** (the `Authenticator`/`Tenant` pair for
> principals established by an HTTP credential, `Hello`'s flags for extensions) and requires
> one policy across both, which is the shape A25's M5 half inherits. **Docs 16 and
> 19** are the plan-side homes for items 2 and 4 and are both still summaries. **No `Event`
> variant and no fold change, so no golden fixture** — item 2 changes a `Command`'s
> *validation*, not its shape, and the reserved flags are an additive field on `Hello`,
> exactly as the delta predicted.

> ### ✅ 2026-09-18 — A15 applied: selective compression is normative, and the protocol/storage group is **done**
>
> **The third transcription of the day and the last of its group.** A18, A1, A24,
> A14 and A15 have all landed, so the spec's wire format, log format, storage
> layout, identifiers, fold and compression are normative — the whole surface M1's
> protocol crate is built against. **The queue's next group is the engine: A2, A3,
> A4.**
>
> **The mechanism landed exactly as signed** — the per-field `codec` discriminator,
> the config-driven allowlist, the ~1 KiB floor, the configurable level, the single
> `[storage] compress = "off" | "blobs" | "allowlist"` knob and the explicit
> non-searchability trade. **Three of its enumerations did not survive deltas that
> landed after it was drafted**, and each is recorded in A15's banner as a deviation
> rather than folded in silently:
>
> 1. **The codec is named in the `LogHeader`, not in the discriminator.** The signed
>    list was `plain | zstd | flat | flat+zstd`; what landed is **`plain |
>    compressed`** plus `{"codec":"zstd"}` in the header A1 created for file-level
>    properties. A15's own banner pre-authorized generalizing the names, and **U25
>    proposed exactly `plain | compressed` with the codec in config** — but config
>    alone would orphan every record already written the moment the codec changed. The
>    log is append-only, so existing records are never re-encoded and one file lives
>    under one codec for its whole life: a file-level property, in the file's header.
>    **Blobs are the exception and must be** — they live outside the log, cannot
>    inherit its header, so each is self-describing.
> 2. **`flat` left the enum.** It is a representation of a *record*, not an encoding
>    of one *field*, and keeping both axes in one per-field discriminator would let a
>    **format** change masquerade as a **compression** change. It stays reserved as
>    §13.5's possible future binary `Codec` — the inert-stub pattern B7 and A22 use.
> 3. **Two compression targets were invalidated by A1.** The signed allowlist named
>    `ToolOutputDelta` chunks as "the dominant cost" and `ThinkingDelta` beside them;
>    **both are `Live`**, broadcast and never written, so compressing them saves zero
>    bytes on disk. The cost *is* dominant — in the stream, not the log. Restated to
>    their durable carriers: `ToolResult.output` and **`ThinkingEnded.text`**, the
>    whole-block boundary A1 added.

> ### ✅ 2026-09-18 — A14 applied: session organization is normative, and the protocol/storage group is one delta from done
>
> **The second transcription off §3's queue, and the second to grow on application.**
> The signed delta named **two** sections (§3.2, §3.5) and three events; **ten were
> edited** — §3.1, §3.2, §3.3, §3.5, §3.7, §4.3, §4.7, §8.4, §12, §14. The reason is
> the hole B13's own amendment opened: all three signed events carry *membership*
> (which folder a session is in), and nothing in the delta carried what a folder **is**
> — name, parent, order. A folder is a cross-session entity while every `Envelope` is
> scoped to one session, so a folder tree has no log to live in; and B13's motivation
> (a feature too big for one session's context) requires creating the folder *before*
> its sessions exist, which pure membership cannot express.
>
> **Four scoping decisions, all four the user's, taken before the edit.**
>
> 1. **The registry is authoritative for names; membership stays a fold.** `org.json`
>    (§12) is the one file in that layout that is **not** a projection, and B13's Fix-1
>    needed an explicit carve-out saying so. **v1 accepts that a rename reaches no
>    client but its issuer**, which learns it from the `Ack`: §3.7's "never silently
>    stale" promise is now **scoped to a session**, with the registry named as the one
>    exception and the freshness channel left to **A7** (§8.2 surface, not replay
>    semantics) — **U99** ✅ **closed by A7 2026-09-19**. Rejected and recorded: widening
>    `Envelope.session` to make the registry an event stream, which would re-open §3.6's
>    cursor, lock and fencing questions for a second stream that is not append-only anyway.
>    **The rejection held, and the channel that replaced it honours it**: §3.6's `Hint` is a
>    third *frame* kind rather than an event — no `session`, no `seq`, no cursor, never
>    written, never replayed — with `org_version` on the four tree reads as the authority.
> 2. **Registry mutation is a `Command`, and §8.4's controller rule does not reach it.**
>    A `Command` because §8.1's default `dacode` is a TUI with an in-process engine and
>    **no socket** — an HTTP-only registry would be unreachable from the client that
>    ships first and principle 1 would be false for it. Not controller-gated because
>    there is no session to control and an empty folder has no controller at all; any
>    authenticated client may mutate it, since §8.3 has no users and no roles and
>    inventing a principal here would be a capability system in all but name. The three
>    *membership* commands joined §8.4's controller-only list.
> 3. **`org.json`, atomic, in §12**, with the conflict rule stated where both files are
>    described: names → the registry, membership → the log. `meta.json`'s comment
>    corrected — it *caches* `SessionInfo`, whose truth stays the log.
> 4. **One op-carrying `Org { op: OrgOp }` rather than seven registry commands**, on
>    `TaskUpdated`'s own argument: one golden fixture covers the subsystem at no loss of
>    expressiveness. **The three membership events were left exactly as signed** —
>    collapsing those too would deviate from a signed delta. Sub-decision forced by the
>    existing `Ack`: **ids are caller-allocated**, because `Ack` has no payload slot and
>    the registry has no log, so there is no channel to return a new id in.
>
> **Two fold-ins the delta did not mention.** **Fix-2 landed normatively in §4.7**, not
> only in doc 06: B13 assigned the worktree derivation to the plan doc, but the spec may
> not cite a plan doc (U91) and a rule §14 must test has to be normative somewhere.
> **§14's fixture obligation is discharged by derivation** — A1's rule makes the durable
> subset self-maintaining, so the three events acquired *log* fixtures with no list to
> update — plus two new engine tests: *a rename is not an event* and *a sandboxed
> session derives to the main repository*.
>

> ### **🧠 MANDATORY BRAINSTORM BEFORE BUILDING THE CORE THREE**
>
> **The main agentic loop, the built-in agents and the built-in tools must each
> get a dedicated brainstorm/design pass with the user before implementation
> starts on them. Do not write them straight from the current spec text.**
>
> These three are where dacode's behaviour is actually decided — every other
> component is plumbing that serves them. The spec describes their *shape*
> (§4.2 loop, §4.3 tool trait, §5.2 agents) but not their *content*: which
> built-in agents ship, what each one's prompt and permission scope is, which
> built-in tools exist, what their arg schemas and concurrency keys are, and how
> the loop's guard set is tuned. Those are product decisions, not derivations,
> and guessing them produces an agent that feels wrong in ways that are
> expensive to retrofit.
>
> **Tracked as explicit items in §5** (M1: loop, built-in tools · M2: built-in
> agents). Each carries a `brainstorm first` marker; the marker is removed only
> when the session has happened and its outcome is written into the relevant
> feature doc.
>
> Input the brainstorm should start from, already gathered: the four
> cross-harness surveys in
> [`.agents/knowledge/reference-harnesses/`](../../.agents/knowledge/reference-harnesses/),
> plus delta [A3](appendices/A-design-deltas.md) (loop guards, synthetic tool
> results, steering vs interrupt), [A2](appendices/A-design-deltas.md)
> (concurrency policy replacing `parallel_safe`),
> [B7](appendices/B-decisions.md) (what `bash:readonly` can and cannot enforce),
> and — for the task-tracking tool specifically — **B15 / A19** with the
> [task-tracking-and-gating](../../.agents/knowledge/reference-harnesses/task-tracking-and-gating.md)
> digest. B15 fixes the *mechanism* (a fold, typed `verify:`, a bounded gate);
> what the brainstorm still owes is the *content*: which kinds ship, what the
> default tree looks like for a plain user session versus an orchestrated one, and
> how hard the gate should be by default.
>
> **✅ 2026-09-17 — the user deferred all three sessions deliberately, and the deferral is
> recorded here so a cold session does not read them as blocking.** They are the *inner
> harness engine*, to be held once the surrounding parts exist. That is compatible with the
> transcription queue under two conditions, and both are obligations on whoever applies a
> delta: **(1)** each transcription lands the approved **shape** and marks
> brainstorm-owned *content* as pending rather than inventing it — which tools ship, the
> guard numbers, `task.reminders_max`, the `todo`/`finding` arg schemas, which agents ship
> and their prompts; §4.8 written self-contained by A19 is the precedent that this works.
> **(2)** the built-in-tools session still precedes **doc 14's deepening and any tool
> implementation** — ~~i.e. before M1's *build* phase, not before its *spec* phase.~~ What the
> deferral costs is bounded: the shape of all three is settled by signed decisions (A2's
> `Concurrency`, A3's guard set, §4.8's mechanism, B17's three engine pieces), so only
> content is exposed.
>

> overstatement is what made M1 look unstartable.** *"Before M1's build phase"* is wider
> than the condition it glosses: **doc 14's deepening and tool implementation are a proper

⚠️ **The finding worth carrying is not in the code: this pass shipped a flake, and the gate matrix as written
cannot see one.** Round 1 was green on every gate and the primary's first `cargo test -p dacode-core` exited
**101** — it measured **10 failures in 628 runs (~1.6%)** across three tests. Both root causes were the same
shape: **a cross-task ordering asserted through an observation point that is not a happens-before edge**
(two tests read `events.jsonl` directly instead of through the flushing helper, because `apply` broadcasts
*inside* `emit` and flushes only after; a third asserted an empty subscriber queue the instant `send`
returned, which holds only while `writer.append().await` happens to yield). ⚠️ **And fixing it introduced a
second flake in the opposite direction.** The re-fence that converted a hang into an assertion bounded a
wait on `LogWriter::shutdown`, whose work runs on a **blocking-pool thread** doing a real drain + flush +
`fsync` — so the bound was spent by the *observer* rather than consumed by the *observed*, and the primary
measured **8/160 failures at 8 concurrent workers** while 1- and 2-worker runs were clean. **The two flakes
were load-sensitive in opposite directions** (the first needed a *fast* writer reply and reproduced at 1
worker; the second needed a *starved* blocking pool and reproduced only at ≥4), which is why one repeat gate
would not have caught both. Fixed: the bound raised 25× on that loop alone with the reason written down, and
the failure message rewritten to name **two** causes and the discriminator between them — after which the
primary re-ran **1020 runs across five load levels, 0 failures**, and 0/240 at the same 8-worker saturation
that had produced 8/160. **The gate matrix gains two additions as a result (tracker f182/f184):** a REPEAT
gate (N≥200 at 1 worker) and a CONTENTION gate (≥4 concurrent whole-suite workers) over whichever modules
carry cross-task ordering, **derived per pass rather than hardcoded** — with the detection floor stated
(1−(1−p)^N: 96% at p=1.6%, 63% at p=0.5%, 18% at p=0.1%), so a green REPEAT reads as "not detected at this N"
and never as "absent".

## 6. Open follow-ups not tied to a milestone

Every item below carries a stable id (`U1`…). Cite the id rather than a line
number — line numbers move on every edit, which is why the `§6:1071` form
`attention.py` used to emit was already stale by the next session. Ids are never
renumbered, so gaps are normal; the maintenance rule above and the
`§6 follow-up ids are unique and complete` check in `attention.py`'s hygiene block
are what hold the scheme.

An item's **action type is declared here too**, in the block below, for the same
reason Appendix A's milestones and Appendix B's action and confidence markers are:
it used to be inferred from three keywords in the item's prose, and that heuristic
was overfitted to the items it was written against. It misfired on a fourth —
**U53, the entry that documents this exact class**, reclassified from `review` to
`ack` because a sentence about an unrelated defect happened to use the word
"sibling". Absence means `review`.

### `dacode-json` (the sibling JSON repo — gates nothing in dacode)

**This section is now the only tracker for these items.** They were carried in
the root `todo-followup.md` handoff note, which has been deleted — its
still-actionable content was folded in here first, verified entry by entry.

None of these block dacode M0. Audit trail — all committed to `dacode-json` `master`:
`90def19` (`RawJson`, opt-in `raw_value` feature) · `53a83d7` (clippy gate fix,
landed first so the WIP went in on green) · `5d4a253` (the orphaned prior-session
WIP: `pull::as_fixed` + `select_object`) · `90b21f9` (`benches/rawjson.rs`).

- [ ] **U1 · Size-table re-measure.** `docs/SIZE.md` + the README extract mix
      `rustc 1.95.0` figures with three rows refreshed on 1.98; neither
      reproduces on the installed `1.98.1`. Needs `tools/size.sh` at `z`, `s` and
      `3` with the toolchain recorded the way `docs/RESULTS.md:12` does. Check
      first whether the 8-bit AVR / 16-bit MSP430 toolchains are even installed.
      Also re-check `docs/SIZE.md`'s `flat`-at-`s`/`3` cells (2 446 → 1 302 and
      3 550 → 1 304 in the WIP) — the one edit in `5d4a253` that moved a number
      for code the WIP did not touch.
- [ ] **U2 · Positional-capture optimization — the biggest remaining win.** Three
      redundant passes, not one: `direct.rs:499-516` validates via `IgnoredAny`,
      then a checked `from_utf8` over the whole span (`:513`), then
      `RawJsonVisitor` has **no `visit_borrowed_str`**, so `visit_str` round-trips
      through `String` into `crate::validate` **again**. At 853 KB, **98% of
      capture's overhead over the ignore floor is that second validation**. A
      trusted already-validated constructor takes capture from 160 → ~410 MiB/s
      (2.6×). Fix all three: add `visit_borrowed_str`, drop the `:513`
      `from_utf8`, add the debug-asserted constructor. **Audit number/string
      strictness first** (`direct`'s `MAX_DEPTH=128` is already stricter than
      `strict`'s `STACK_MAX=256`). Keep the path `unsafe`-free — it is today;
      `direct.rs:220`'s neighbouring `from_utf8_unchecked` is *not* the model.
      **⚠️ Do not extend the trusted constructor to the *pool* path.** There the
      validate is **not** redundant: a faithful-parser `Doc` can `to_json` to
      invalid JSON. Assuming otherwise was the med-severity bug found and fixed
      during `90def19`'s review — trusting pool-path bytes re-opens it. Note also
      that `validate` re-checks UTF-8 for non-ASCII (`strict.rs:519`), which is
      the fourth pass in the chain.
- [ ] **U3 · `crate::validate` allocates per call** (`api.rs:276` builds a fresh
      `StrictParser`) — 20 allocations for one 873 KB validate, contradicting
      `api.rs:162-163`'s "allocates nothing but the output". A reused pre-sized
      parser is 0 allocations and ~11% faster.
- [ ] **U4 · Field-skip path is 26% slower than `serde_json`'s** (417 vs 530 MiB/s at
      853 KB). `direct.rs:443-447` routes `{`/`[` through `deserialize_any` +
      serde's `MapAccess` instead of a dedicated skip. Capture inherits this as
      its floor, so fixing it lifts the `raw_value` story too.
- [ ] **U5 · Borrowed `&RawJson` form?** Owned-only (`Box<str>`) is right for
      store-and-re-emit events. Add a borrowed zero-copy form only if a hot
      transient splice path appears.
- [ ] **U6 · `stream` deserializer capture** — currently a clean error. Wire it
      byte-exact only if dacode uses `stream::from_slice_with` for events.
- [ ] **U7 · Fuzz the `RawJson` capture path** before a release bumps the version
      dacode pins.
- [x] **U8 · dacode will depend on `dacode-json` with `features = ["raw_value"]`** once the
      protocol crate exists (M1). Until then `RawJson` has no in-tree consumer.
      ✅ **DISCHARGED 2026-09-20 by M1.2's commit**: `dacode-json` is the first of the
      protocol crate's four dependencies, `raw_value` on, entering through a path
      entry in the root `[workspace.dependencies]` (doc 01 §1.9's corrected
      mechanism — `[patch]` cannot rewrite a never-published crate), and `RawJson`
      is re-exported flat from `dacode_protocol` so no client needs its own
      dacode-json edge for a public field type (tracker f130). The golden fixtures
      pin its byte-exact splice — `snapshot.json` deliberately carries a
      reversed-key raw value so a canonicalizing encoder *fails* the suite.

#### Measured baseline — what may be quoted, and what may not

[B1](appendices/B-decisions.md) and delta
[A16](appendices/A-design-deltas.md) both justify the hybrid strategy with these
numbers, so they are recorded here rather than left in a chat log. Source:
`benches/rawjson.rs` at `90b21f9`.

Host `darwin/arm64`, `rustc 1.98.1`, `[profile.bench] opt-level=3 lto="fat"
codegen-units=1`, criterion 0.5.1, `sample_size(30)`, corpus
`corpus::geo_int(_, 0xA7C5)`.

| 853 KB payload | splice | re-encode (tree) | ignore floor | tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **13.9 µs / 57–59 GiB/s** | 1.57–1.90 ms / 462–532 MiB/s | 2.00 ms / 417 MiB/s | 7.85 ms / 106 MiB/s |

- Splice is **≈110× faster than re-encoding** (112–118× across four runs) against
  `serde_json`'s own serializer over the same tree — the strongest opponent
  measured, hence the conservative quote. **≈130×** against `dacode-json`'s
  serializer over that tree. `dacode-json` driving a foreign enum is **8–15%** slower
  than `serde_json` driving its own.
- The win is **per-byte, not per-value**: marginal ratio 141× (2.3→35 KB) then
  129× (35→853 KB).
- **Capture is 1.2–1.5× cheaper than building a tree** (1.24/1.24/1.50×) and stays
  byte-exact where the tree is not; **2 inherent allocations vs the tree's
  114 080**.
- Native-DOM fairness: per-turn re-emit from a retained pool doc (`Value::to_json`)
  **5.26 ms** vs `serde_json::to_vec` of a retained tree **1.66 ms** vs the splice
  **13.9 µs** = **378×**. One-time acquisition: `parse + to_json` **8.10 ms**,
  `parse + RawJson::from_doc` **11.29 ms**.

**Methodology constraint — both arms of any ratio must come from one build.** A
single edit to the bench file moved an in-process measurement 14.43 → 17.57 µs.
`tools/isolate.sh` and a shared criterion process agree to ~0.3% *within* a build.

**Do NOT quote these — each was retracted during review:**

- "25% slower in the shared criterion process"
- "10–15%" (the correct figure is 8–15%)
- "capture costs 2.6× a tree" — the 2.6× is capture vs the *ignore floor*, and
  98% of that gap is the redundant second validate, not the copy
- "capture inherently allocates 22 objects" — 2 are inherent, 20 belong to the
  redundant pass
- group-(a) MiB/s compared against group-(b) MiB/s — different denominators
  (output-byte vs input-byte)
- anything about `serde_json`'s own `RawValue` — its `raw_value` feature is off
  and was never measured
- the *total* ratio climbing ~50× → ~130× as evidence of scaling — that is the
  splice arm's ~53 ns loop floor falling away (61% of its 2 KB time, 0.4% at
  853 KB)

### Repo hygiene traps

- **`tools/agents-index.py` self-stales on every commit, and that is a benign
  fixpoint — not drift.** The root `AGENTS.md` "lag" count includes all commits,
  so regenerating `INDEX.md` produces a commit that itself makes `INDEX.md`
  stale.   **The integrity hash is what matters; do not chase `--check` to green by
  re-committing.** Promote this to `.agents/pitfalls.md` at the next milestone.
- **The depth grep counted *descriptions* of the marker, not just bearers of it —
  and `--exclude=TODO.md` had only patched one instance.** The marker is the full
  phrase `migrated summary; expand during implementation` inside an HTML comment,
  but the documented command grepped the two words, so any prose mentioning the
  marker counted as carrying it. This bit during the B1 pass: an Appendix B banner
  saying doc 14 was "still a migrated summary" moved §4's count from 27 to 28.
  Fixed by grepping the full phrase (maintenance rule + §4 here, and
  `dacode-imp-next` hard rule 5). **Rule for future prose: describe the marker
  without quoting its full phrase.** The earlier `f14`/`t30` fix added
  `--exclude=TODO.md` for this same bug class and stopped at the one file that had
  shown it; the durable fix is the phrase, not a longer exclude list.
- **Appending a resolution suffix to a heading silently breaks every in-page
  anchor pointing at it.** The appendices' convention is to retitle on
  resolution — `### A18 — …` becomes `### A18 — … — ✅ **APPLIED 2026-09-12**` —
  and GitHub's slug is derived from the whole heading, so the anchor changes with
  it. Caught during the A18/B4 pass: A1's cross-reference to A18 was the **only**
  in-page anchor in the repo, and it broke the moment A18 was applied. Seven
  appendix headings already carry such a suffix, so any new anchor to a delta or
  decision is broken-on-arrival by design. **Rule: cross-reference deltas and
  decisions as plain text ("A18", "B4"), never as `](#…)` anchors.** They are
  short, greppable identifiers in the same file; the anchor bought nothing and
  cost a silent breakage. `tools/check-links.py` does validate in-page anchors,
  so this is caught — but only if the link exists to be caught, and only at the
  next run.
  **Same class as the marker trap above, and worth naming as one rule: a status
  flip must not mutate a form something else reads mechanically** — whether that
  is a grep marker, a heading slug, or a count in a table.
- [ ] **U9 · The field-skip gap deserves a row in dacode-json's `docs/RESULTS.md`** if it
      is real and stays — `benches/rawjson.rs` group `rawjson_capture_de` is
      currently the only place it is visible.

- [x] **U31 · `tools/tasks.py check` cannot express a standing goal, so a long-lived

      explicitly non-blocking. The design phase has a legitimately standing goal —
      the decision pass over the remaining B-decisions and A-deltas — open for
      weeks. A gate that is always red gets ignored, which is the failure mode the
      mandatory-checker rule exists to prevent. The workaround (recording in that
      goal's `verify` field that `OPEN g14` is the expected steady state) is now
      retired: **`--status standing` exists**, `check` prints it as `STAND` and
      exits 0, and g14 is set to it.

      suppresses a gate is worse than no status.** (1) A standing goal is still
      *printed* — dropping it from the output is how a long-running programme stops
      being looked at. (2) It still needs a `verify`, holding the per-delivery
      condition rather than a completion test; `TBD` blocks. (3) **Only goals may
      be standing** — applied to a task it is just a way to dodge the gate, so both
      `set` and `check` refuse it (`check` is the backstop because the tracker is a
      file in the worktree and can be hand-edited). (4) **It needs a `note` saying
      why it cannot close**, the same rule `blocked` already had. Review found this
      one: as first written, marking a goal standing was *cheaper* than marking it
      done — `done` demands evidence and a decided verify, standing demanded
      nothing and still turned the gate green. An exemption from a gate that costs
      less than satisfying the gate is not an exemption, it is a bypass.
      Six cases negative-tested: refusal on a task and on a finding, a hand-edited
      standing task, a standing goal with `TBD` verify, and a standing goal with no
      note both via `set` and hand-edited.

      answer to it.** §16.6 is the same gap in the *product* — design §4.8's
      completion gate reddens while a `Goal` is unclosed, with only `Blocked` and
      `WontFix` exempt — and inventing a `TaskStatus::Standing` there would exceed
      B15's signed-off text. What the tool fix contributes is **evidence**: the
      four properties above are what a working standing status turned out to need,
      which is a better input to §16.6 than the abstract argument was. Recorded
      against f31 in the tracker.

### From a client-transport question (session 5)

Asked as "how do TUI/web clients talk to `serve` — WebSocket or pub/sub, what is
best for fast notifications?" It surfaced two spec gaps, first recorded as an
amendment to [B4](appendices/B-decisions.md)'s dossier and then **split out as
delta [A18](appendices/A-design-deltas.md)** — because both are
transport-independent, so they need not wait on B4, which is by its own account
the most taste-driven decision in the set. **That split paid off: A18 and B4 were
signed off together the same day, A18 first**, which reduced B4 to the pure
transport choice and left §3.6 needing no edit at all.

- [x] **U32 · §3.7's "No gap, no duplicate" was asserted, not earned — FIXED by A18.**
      that would earn it lives only in a summary-depth plan doc.** §4.1 picks "a
      broadcast channel per session" and stops there; `tokio::sync::broadcast`
      **drops the oldest messages when a receiver lags** (`RecvError::Lagged`),
      so the primitive the spec already chose is lossy under a slow consumer and
      §3.7's flat claim is false as written.
      [07-session-registry](part2-engine/07-session-registry.md):16 does call for
      "a bounded queue and explicit drop/backpressure policy … a slow client must
      not stall the engine", but that is not where an implementer looks for a
      correctness invariant. **A18's replacement §3.7 text is now in the spec**,
      along with the two limits that turned out to be one invariant: the
      in-memory replay window (5 000) must exceed the subscriber queue depth
      (256), or a client lagging far enough to be dropped also falls outside
      cheap replay and pays a disk read to recover. Note this was *not* an
      argument for unbounded queues — those let one stalled browser tab apply
      backpressure to the engine, trading recoverable staleness for an
      unrecoverable hang. §4.1 gained the one-sentence bounded-channel rule and
      §14 gained the two tests that can actually fail on it (fold-idempotence
      over `seq`, and a lagged subscriber that must resync to the same folded
      state) — the §14 half went slightly beyond A18's literal proposal, because
      an untested invariant is how §3.7 acquired a false guarantee to begin with,
      and it is recorded as a scoping decision in A18's banner.
- [ ] **U33 · Decide the HTTP version deliberately — new, owed by M3.** B4's resolution
      surfaced it. Browsers cap concurrent connections per origin (~6 under
      HTTP/1.1). That is usually discussed as an SSE problem, but it bites
      whichever live transport is chosen: several dashboard tabs can exhaust the
      budget against §8.2's HTTP endpoints, which carry the files, diffs and
      blobs the "large payloads are HTTP" split depends on. Serving HTTP/2
      removes the cap. Small decision, but it should be *made* rather than
      inherited from whatever the HTTP crate defaults to — recorded in
      [B4](appendices/B-decisions.md)'s banner and
      [19](part4-hosts-clients/19-server-gateway.md).
- [ ] **U34 · The default TUI is in-process, and doc 19's framing hides it.** §8.1's
      four process models mean plain `dacode` touches `SessionRegistry` directly
      (§4.1) and receives events over the per-session broadcast channel — no
      socket, no serialization. Only `attach` and the web UI have a transport
      question at all. Doc 19's now-resolved `[DECISION] WS vs SSE` block invited
      the wrong mental model (every client behind a wire); when 19 is deepened at
      M3, lead with the locality split, then the transport. **Still open**, and
      not a doc-19 edit only: §8.1 lists the four process models but no section
      says in so many words that the *default* TUI never touches a socket, which
      is why the question reads as bigger than it is.
- [ ] **U35 · For notification latency, the transport is close to the least of it.**
      WS and SSE are both push over a persistent connection and both are
      sub-millisecond on localhost, against a provider round-trip measured in
      seconds. What actually decides it: **A1's two-tier model** (live deltas
      never persisted, so the hot path avoids §3.6's fsync on
      `TurnFinished`/`ToolResult`/request-answer) — ✅ **normative since 2026-09-18,
      so this is no longer a prediction about a delta but a property of §3.2/§3.6** —
      the **bounded fan-out** above,
      and **client-side ≤16 ms coalescing** (the doc-22 deepening item in §6's
      session-3b list). Worth saying plainly whenever this question recurs,
      because "WS vs SSE" reads like the latency decision and is not.

### From losing the thread (session 6, third pass)

The user's report was *"I currently lose the tracking. From where came 16.6."*
That is a defect in the plan's own ergonomics, not in their attention: spec §16
item 6 was created, committed, and recorded in **three** places (the spec, B15's
banner, Appendix A's applied-deltas row) and was still invisible to the one person
who had to act on it. Recording a decision correctly is not the same as surfacing
it.

- [x] **U51 · `tools/attention.py` — one prioritized view of everything needing the
      user's decision. BUILT.** Reads all five sources (Appendix B's summary
      table, Appendix A's index, the spec's §16, this file's §6 unchecked items,
      the 🧠 brainstorm gates) plus the task tracker's open debt and user-gates,
      and renders one table to stdout and `.agents/cache/ATTENTION.md`
      (**gitignored** — a rendering of committed state, never a source of it).
      Priority is **derived, not hand-assigned**: from which milestone the item
      gates, via the doc→milestone map in
      [31-ci-milestones](part6-quality/31-ci-milestones.md) (M0/M1 → P0, M2/M3 →
      P1, M4+ → P2, none → P3), so it stays honest as the board changes. The
      `Do` column separates **vote** / **measure** / **session** / **review** /
      **ack**, because "sign off" is not one thing — B12 needs a benchmark, four
      items need a sitting-down design session, and neither is a vote.
      `--max-priority N` narrows, `--json` is machine-readable, `--check` exits 1
      on any P0 so it can gate a delivery. Added to `AGENTS.md`'s Key Files table
      and to its committing checklist, so an agent reports "nothing needs your
      input" only after running it.
- [ ] **U52 · The count it reported is itself a finding worth acting on: 65 open items,
      14 of them P0.** Four need a design *session*, one needs a *measurement*, 26
      need a vote, 33 are unowned follow-ups. That is not a list a person holds in
      their head, and the P0 set is mostly M1's blockers — so **M0 is still the
      right next step** (it is gated on nothing), but M1 cannot start until a chunk
      of that 14 is cleared. Worth deciding whether to batch the votes (B3, B5,
      B7, B14 are all `accept`-recommended at high confidence and all gate M1) in
      one pass rather than one at a time.
- [ ] **U53 · `attention.py` scrapes markdown, so it breaks silently when the docs'
      shapes change.** Four bugs were found by running it against the real docs and
      spot-checking rows against known ground truth, not by reading the code: doc
      numbers are zero-padded in Appendix B's `Gates` column (`05`) but not in the
      milestone table (`5`), which silently reported "gates no milestone" for
      B3/B12/B13; a `re.S` regex swallowed the file so only 1 of 4 brainstorm gates
      appeared; B12's signal is written `**measured** decision`, so matching raw
      markdown mislabelled the one decision needing a benchmark as a vote; and
      A-deltas were held behind *already-resolved* B-decisions. **Generalises: a
      doc-scraping tool needs its output checked against ground truth, not just a
      zero exit code.** The durable fix would be machine-readable front matter on
      the appendix tables instead of scraping prose — worth doing if this tool
      survives another milestone.
      **An eighth instance was found while rendering B19 (session 11), and it is the
      first one that misinforms rather than merely mis-sorts.**
      `why_from_confidence` tests `"low" in confidence.lower()` — a *substring* match
      over the whole cell — so B19's three-way cell (`high (prevention must precede
      creation) / med (the args check) / low (how wide the injected set goes)`)
      rendered as **"confidence marked LOW — genuinely your taste, not the
      evidence"**. That is not a wrong priority, it is a wrong *characterisation*:
      B19's central claim is forced by the append-only log, and telling the reader it
      is a taste call invites them to skip the evidence. Two defects in one line —
      the substring match, which would also fire on "follow", "below" or "allow" in

      matcher now takes `\b(high|med|low)\b` *tokens* and reads the **first** as the
